reason: I adopt the opinion. S1 and S4 correctly pin 103.1 as naming a single 'loser' with no way to pick among two, a real gap (my tournament-document check found MTR 2.2 only mirrors 103.1 for two players, so nothing fills it). S2 (903.2: a three-player Commander game is multiplayer, default Free-for-All) and S3 (800.4: players leave one after another, so losers are ordered in time) hold. Stipulation S5 is stated as the case words it. It fits inside 103.1 because the chooser is always a player who lost (a winner is never among the losers, ties are only among losers). The earlier refutations (team games via 104.2c, winner-choosing fallback, turn-order ambiguity) are answered by limiting to free-for-all (806.1) and dropping turn order. S6 leaves 103.1's draw sentence untouched, and 104.4a sends simultaneous loss of all remaining players to that draw sentence, so the tie-break never meets a drawn game. The holding matches the rule word for word. I accept it as the rule.

evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.
If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.
multiplayer games can continue after one or more players have left the game.
A Commander game may be a two-player game or a multiplayer game.
In Free-for-All multiplayer games, a group of players compete as individuals against each other.
If all the players remaining in a game lose simultaneously, the game is a draw.
